title: House band at the Dew Drop
summary: Playing shows at the Dew Drop, Big Joe Turner, dancers, Cecil Gant; Toussaint and Booker outside.

story.theme_name: Gangsters, bootleggers and rough clubs of Prohibition
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Do you remember what year that was?
Around 50, no, it was in the 40s. Around 40, 40, around 48. And were you, what, the term, the house band? Yeah.
At the Dewdrop? Yeah. At the Dewdrop? Okay. And so what, could you tell me how the house band worked at the Dewdrop? Because I know it's different than at other clubs.

Yeah, but you know like all these musicians that they're making a lot over, because they played at the Dewdrop. Now when I was playing at the Dewdrop, a guy like Alan Toussaint and Booker. James Booker? James Booker? Yeah. James Booker? Yeah. They were little boys. They didn't play at the Dewdrop during the time I was playing there. They used to hang around and be outside. They still spend most of the time outside listening to the musicians, you know. But the way they advertised them, like they was a part of the thing that made the Dewdrop.
Could you tell me what the house band did at the Dewdrop? I mean, what you all?

We had to play shows. Right. We played some dance numbers, then after that they had shows to come out. We had to play a show. And they had some good shows there. Dancers, singers. That's when I first met Big Joe Turner. He came there as a singer. Then one on the Harris. Then they had Vaughn and Great Truth. They were dancers. They had some nice routines they did. And there was a guy who made a record, a hit record while he was in the service, private, Cecil Gaint. You ever hear of him? Yeah. He came there and we played for him. Paul, yeah, I played with Ray Charles too. I got with Ray Charles band in 1957. And I was the musical director then.
